summary:
We developed AgroKairos, an open-source agroclimatic decision-support web platform and FastAPI service powered by 25 years of NASA Earth observations (NASA GPM IMERG V07 precipitation and NASA POWER / MERRA-2 root-zone soil moisture and temperature, 2000–2024) for Angola's Central Plateau across Huambo, Bié, and Huíla (33 municipalities).

    To address the "Be an Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, AgroKairos translates statistical Earth-system trend detection (Mann-Kendall trends, Kaplan-Meier rainy-season onset P50/P90 quantiles, and Wilson 90% confidence false-start risk intervals) into three synchronized bilingual tools: an interactive provincial and municipal viability map, a 52-week radial and monthly phase-colored sowing cycle explorer, and a detailed agronomic consultation strictly separating 25-year NASA climatology from complementary Open-Meteo and ECMWF forecasts.

    This work is important because climate variability increasingly triggers deceptive early rains followed by dry spells that destroy newly germinated seeds. By alerting smallholder farmers and rural extension officers when rainfall onset is unstable, AgroKairos helps prevent costly replanting, protects harvests for Maize, Common Bean, Soybean, Cassava, and Rice, strengthens rural food security, and provides a replicable scientific template for other rain-fed regions.
details:
Problem & Local Impact

In Angola's Central Plateau (Huambo, Bié, and Huíla), rain-fed smallholder farming sustains local food security. However, climate variability causes deceptive early rainfall events ("false starts") followed by dry spells that destroy germinated seeds, forcing vulnerable families to replant at high cost or lose their harvest.

What AgroKairos Does

AgroKairos bridges NASA satellite Earth observations and practical field decisions through three synchronized, mobile-friendly interfaces (available in English and Angolan Portuguese):

1. Interactive Provincial & Municipal Map (/mapa): Displays Angola and zooms into the 33 municipalities of Huambo (11), Bié (9), and Huíla (13), color-coding deterministic agroclimatic readiness (FAVORAVEL / Favorable, AGUARDAR/ Wait, DESFAVORAVEL / Unfavorable) for each crop and reference date.

2. 52-Week & Monthly Sowing Cycle Explorer (/ciclo): Features a radial 52-ISO-week crop cycle ring and a phase-colored monthly calendar showing historical sowing suitability (High >=65%, Moderate/Caution 35–64%, Low/Off-season <35%), root-zone moisture reserves, and false-start risk intervals—strictly synchronized with map selections.

3. Detailed Agronomic Consultation (/consulta): Combines deterministic rule evaluation (POST /api/v1/evaluate) with bilingual farmer extension guidance (POST /api/v1/advisory) and explicit fallback notices whenever live meteorological data is replaced by 2000–2024 climatology.

Scientific Methodology ("Rule of Gold")

- Rainy-Season Onset & False-Start Protection (ciclo_diario.py v0.3.0): Processes 25 seasonal NASA GPM IMERG V07 NetCDF datasets (2000–2024) using Kaplan-Meier onset quantiles (P50/P90) and false-start risk curves with conservative Wilson 90% confidence intervals (IC90), clamped between 5% and 95% so the system never presents false 0% or 100% certainty.

- Soil & Thermal Baselines: Extracts 25-year daily NASA POWER / MERRA-2 root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT) and temperature (T2M) baselines, monthly percentiles (P25/P50/P75), 52-week crop curves, and Mann-Kendall climate trend tests.

- Strict Provenance Separation: Short-term forecasts (Open-Meteo 16-day) and 6-month seasonal outlooks (ECMWF SEAS5) are kept separate from 25-year NASA historical baselines and explicitly labeled in the UI and API.

Technology Stack

- Frontend: React 19, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS 4, custom deterministic SVG geo-projection (ADM1 & ADM2 boundaries), Vitest + Testing Library (431 automated tests), ESLint, hosted on Netlify.

- Backend: Python FastAPI REST API, Pandas/SciPy/Pydantic v2, automated pytest suite, hosted on Render.

- Public Endpoints: https://detetive-da-chuva.onrender.com (e.g., GET /api/v1/map-overview, GET /api/v1/optimal-planting, GET /api/v1/municipalities, POST /api/v1/evaluate, POST /api/v1/advisory, GET /compliance).
